title: The Very Large Telescope snaps a stellar nursery and celebrates fifteen years of operations
caption: The stellar nursery IC 2944 and the Thackeray globules, imaged by the Very Large Telescope
celestial: IC 2944, IC 2948 · constellation Centaurus · about 6500 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Ranked #3 on ESO’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: Thick, dark clouds of dust stand in silhouette against the pale pink glow of gas in this view of IC 2944, a stellar nursery. The dark clumps are known as the Thackeray globules.
ESO released it to mark 15 years of operations for its Very Large Telescope. Nearby hot young stars are bombarding the globules with fierce ultraviolet radiation.

The globules are in trouble. The radiation is wearing them away and breaking them into fragments, much as lumps of butter would on a hot frying pan. Dense clouds like these can sometimes collapse to form new stars, but these ones are unlikely to get the chance. They will probably be destroyed first, worn down by the radiation of their hot young neighbours before any stars can form inside them.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (7.18 x 7.18 arcminutes) and distance (6500 light years), the frame spans roughly 14 × 14 light-years. Its light set out about 6,500 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This visible-light image was made with the FORS1 instrument on ESO's Very Large Telescope, using blue, visual and red filters plus filters for glowing oxygen and hydrogen. The source does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: The nebula's faint glow is far too dim to see in this colour and detail by eye. Long exposures gather far more light.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: IC 2944 lies about 6500 light-years away in the constellation Centaurus. The image was made with the FORS1 instrument, using filters including ones that isolate the glow of oxygen and hydrogen.
alt: Dark clumps of dust silhouetted against pale pink glowing gas.
